newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower as Egypt bypasses U.S.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower as Egypt bypasses U.S.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on news Egypt bought wheat from Australia, Argentina and France rather than the United States, traders said.
"Egypt took wheat from everyone else so we'll (U.S.) have to scrounge out some business," said O'Connor and Co's Ron Kucha.
Egypt over the weekend bought 600,000 tonnes of wheat with 200,000 coming from Australia, 250,000 from Argentina and 150,000 from France, Cairo trade sources said.
Some said it was not a surprise Egypt bypassed the U.S. and noted Friday's sharp break in KCBT and MGE wheat was linked to expectations that Egypt would not buy U.S. supplies.
"That's what broke it Friday, we weren't competitive (pricewise)," said Skip Searcy, of FIMAT Futures.
The December contract early in the session dropped below first support at $3.94 per bushel and reached a session low of $3.91 but rebounded late to that first chart plateau at $3.94.
Technicians said the four and 20-day moving averages were beginning to give off bullish flags and December's daily relative strength index (RSI) closed at 55 points.
Wheat futures closed 3-1/4 to six cents per bushel lower, with December down 3-1/4 at $3.94.
Wheat also was pressured by a lower-than-expected number in USDA's weekly export inspections report.
USDA Monday said 14.529 million bushels of wheat were inspected for export during the week ended November 14. That tally was below trade estimates which ranged from 15 million to 20 million bushels.
Overall good weather for the U.S. winter wheat crop including beneficial moisture recently in the key U.S. Plains hard red winter region, also weighed on the market.
Dean Witter Reynolds sold one million bushels of March, Term Commodities bought 2.5 million March and Cargill Inc bought one million bushels of December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 12,000, down from 15,463 Friday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, Cargill Investor Services sold 500 March $4.20 calls at five cents, Rosenthal Collins bought 100 March $4.20 calls at 5-1/4 cents and Cargill Investor Services sold 100 March $3.90 calls at 12-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,000, up from 2,958 Friday.
